thread:
ana_rodriguez: Heads-up — HorizonBank POC kickoff. They want a drop-in replacement for their current vendor endpoint (legacy-api.example.com/v1/generate). Scope: prompt parity + deterministic deltas, response normalization, and pricing parity. Timeline = 2w. Need SE + Security to weigh in on blockers and an exec-summary for pricing.

mike_chen: Quick q — do we have their sample request/response corpus? shape matters (single prompt vs messages array). Also what latency SLO are they expecting? p95 target?

ana_rodriguez: They've sent a sample zip (shared in the onboarding drive). Payloads are mostly chat-like: [{role,user,content}] and a few legacy single-prompt calls. They mentioned 200ms p95 as ideal but said they'll accept up to 500ms for edge cases.

sophie_lee: Proposed POC plan:
1) Build a tiny "compat shim" that accepts their legacy payload and translates to Redwood chat/generation API.
2) Run an eval harness of ~500 prompts from their corpus to measure response delta (semantic and token delta).
3) Add a response-normalizer step to strip/standardize metadata and enforce deterministic topn for parity tests.
4) Surface token-accounting differences and produce an example billing delta for them.

sophie_lee: Quick mapping example to share with their engineers:
```
# incoming legacy
{"prompt": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 150}
# shim -> Redwood
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize..."}],
  "max_tokens": 150
}
```
This preserves intent but normalizes the envelope.

mike_chen: For parity testing we should lock randomness: temperature=0, top_p=1, deterministic sampling where possible. Also capture full tokenization so we can show where token counts diverge.

jamal_patel: Security checklist items from my side:
- Confirm data residency (they require EU residency for PII)
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key)
- Audit logs: per-request headers persisted for 90 days
- SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence + pen-test report
I'll start the security questionnaire draft — need the POC network IP ranges for allowlist.

ana_rodriguez: They will give us an allowlist for staging. Also asked about on-prem/private deployment later — flagging for Private team.

mike_chen: On pricing: customer expects a simple per-call parity price (they fear token accounting volatility). We should produce two artifacts:
- Per-invocation parity quote (flat per-call) for migration phase
- Token-based comparison showing our expected unit cost at their throughput
I can prepare a small spreadsheet with three example requests from their corpus to illustrate.

sophie_lee: I'll own the eval harness + normalization code. Plan to run baseline against vendor and Redwood and produce a diff report that includes:
- semantic similarity score (embedding-based)
- token delta and estimated cost
- top-3 failure cases (formatting, hallucination, truncation)

ana_rodriguez: Can we commit to a smoke by EOD Wednesday? horizonbk engineering prefers early-morning window (07:00-09:00 UTC).

mike_chen: EOD Wed smoke is doable. I'll provision a small Redwood staging model instance and wire the shim. Deploy instructions I'll paste in the thread when ready.

deploy-bot: staging environment "hb-poc-staging" created in us-west-2. SSH jump box and allowlist placeholders added.

jamal_patel: Sending the first-pass security answers in a doc by tomorrow. Need to confirm KMS flow with infra.

sophie_lee: For the response-normalizer: I'll include a canonicalizer that removes vendor-specific debug fields, normalizes whitespace, and enforces a fixed JSON schema (title, body, metadata). That usually knocks down false-positive deltas.

ana_rodriguez: Thanks — I'll push this plan to the customer and schedule the engineering sync for Thu 08:00 UTC. Also cc'ing finance for the ad-hoc per-call quote.

mike_chen: One more note — if we see consistent token inflation on their corpus vs vendor, recommend quantized model variant + batching changes. Will report if that happens.

sophie_lee: :thumbsup: will prepare PR for shim + harness and post link here.

ana_rodriguez: Great. Team — any enterprise blockers not covered?

jamal_patel: Blocker checklist: KMS agreement, EU residency attestation, and a signed DPA. If those look good, no blockers from security.

ana_rodriguez: Perfect. I'll track DPA with legal. Marking this thread as active.
